def: A storage protocol and architecture (subsystem, controllers, namespaces, paired submission/completion queues, commands and completions) defined by the NVM Express specification family. It runs over PCIe, RDMA or TCP transports.

The binding that defines how NVMe uses PCIe: registers memory-mapped in BAR0, doorbells from offset 1000h, queues and data in host memory reached by device DMA, PRP/SGL rules and interrupt use. Specified in the NVMe over PCIe Transport Specification (1.4 in the 2026 set).
The NVMe entity that contains one or more controllers, zero or more namespaces and one or more ports, plus the media. Named by its subsystem NQN (SUBNQN).

The interface between a host and an NVM subsystem: it owns properties (registers), the admin queue, I/O queues, doorbells and controller state, and processes commands for attached namespaces. Identified by CNTLID within the subsystem.

A formatted quantity of non-volatile storage associated with one I/O command set and identified by an NSID within the subsystem. For the NVM Command Set it is an array of logical blocks. Attached to zero or more controllers.
The number that names a namespace within an NVM subsystem; valid values are 1 to NN (Identify Controller). 0 is not a namespace; FFFFFFFFh is a broadcast value where a command allows it.
A 16-bit identifier, unique within an NVM subsystem, reported in Identify Controller. Fixed on PCIe; may be allocated dynamically on fabrics.
A globally unique name string for an NVM subsystem (SUBNQN) or a host (host NQN).
A vocabulary of commands with defined meaning. The Admin Command Set (in the Base Specification) manages controllers; I/O command sets (NVM, ZNS, KV, SLM, Computational Programs) act on namespaces.
The value naming the I/O command set a namespace uses: 00h NVM, 01h Key Value, 02h Zoned Namespace (others defined in the Base Specification).
The mechanism that carries NVMe commands, data and completions between host and controller: memory-based (PCIe) or message-based (RDMA, TCP; FC-NVMe is defined by INCITS T11).
The core NVM Express document (Revision 2.4 in the August 2026 set): architecture, controller properties, queueing model, Admin Command Set, common status codes, logs, features and fabrics behaviour.
An NVMe controller that supports I/O queues and gives a host access to namespaces for I/O.
An NVMe controller that manages an NVM subsystem (e.g. namespace or virtualization management) and has an admin queue but no I/O queues.
An NVMe over Fabrics controller that reports, through the Discovery Log Page, which NVM subsystems are reachable through which ports.
A 64-byte NVMe command placed in a submission queue: CDW0 (opcode, CID), NSID, data pointer and command-specific dwords.
A 16-byte completion posted by the controller: command-specific result, SQ head and ID, CID, Phase Tag and Status field.
A circular queue of SQEs, written by the host and consumed by the controller; on PCIe it normally lives in host memory.
A circular queue of CQEs, written by the controller and consumed by the host; one CQ may serve several SQs.
A controller register the host writes to publish a new SQ tail or CQ head. On PCIe, SQyTDBL is at BAR0 + 1000h + 2y × (4 << CAP.DSTRD) and CQyHDBL one stride later.
Bit 16 of CQE DW3, inverted by the controller on each pass through the CQ, so the host can tell new entries from old ones without reading a register.
A 16-bit value in CDW0 chosen by the host, unique among outstanding commands in one SQ, echoed in the CQE to match completion to command.
64-bit read-only controller register at offset 00h: MQES, CQR, AMS, TO, DSTRD, NSSRS, CSS, BPS, MPSMIN, MPSMAX, PMRS, CMBS and newer fields.
Controller register at offset 08h reporting the Base Specification revision claimed: major (31:16), minor (15:8), tertiary (7:0).
Controller register at offset 14h written by the host: EN, CSS, MPS, AMS, SHN, IOSQES, IOCQES (and CRIME from 2.0).
Controller register at offset 1Ch reporting RDY, CFS, SHST, NSSRO and PP. An all-ones read means the MMIO read failed, not a status.
Controller register at 24h: ASQS (11:0) and ACQS (27:16), the 0's based admin SQ and CQ sizes (2 to 4096 entries).
64-bit controller register at 28h holding the admin SQ base address (bits 63:12).
64-bit controller register at 30h holding the admin CQ base address (bits 63:12).

exp: Interrupt Mask Set / Interrupt Mask Clear
def: Controller registers at 0Ch and 10h used to mask and unmask interrupt vectors with pin-based or MSI interrupts; not used when MSI-X is enabled.
Optional controller register at 20h; writing 4E564D65h ("NVMe") resets the whole NVM subsystem, including (on PCIe) its ports.
CAP bits 15:0, the 0's based maximum number of entries in an I/O queue.
CAP bits 35:32; doorbells are spaced 4 << DSTRD bytes apart starting at BAR0 + 1000h.
CAP bits 31:24: the worst-case time, in 500 ms units, the host should wait for CSTS.RDY to change after changing CC.EN.
CSTS bit 1, set when the controller has a fatal condition it cannot report through a completion; the host must reset the controller.
CSTS bits 3:2: 00b normal, 01b shutdown processing occurring, 10b shutdown processing complete.

Any reset that resets an NVMe controller: Controller Reset (CC.EN 1 to 0), NVM Subsystem Reset, PCIe Conventional Reset, or Function Level Reset. I/O queues and outstanding commands are discarded; namespaces are not affected.
Identify Controller field: the maximum data transfer of one command as a power of two in units of the minimum memory page size (CAP.MPSMIN); 0 means no limit.
Identify Controller field giving the maximum valid NSID, not the number of namespaces that exist.

exp: Namespace Multi-path I/O and Namespace Sharing Capabilities
def: Identify Namespace field indicating whether a namespace may be attached to more than one controller.

exp: Controller Multi-Path I/O and Namespace Sharing Capabilities
def: Identify Controller field indicating whether the subsystem may have multiple ports, multiple controllers, or SR-IOV association.
Optional device memory exposed through a BAR that a host may use for queues or data; described by CMBLOC and CMBSZ.
Optional persistent, byte-addressable device memory exposed through a BAR, described by the PMR registers (1.4 and later).
The PCIe BAR (with BAR1 as its upper half when 64-bit) whose memory range holds the NVMe controller registers and doorbells.
Accessing device registers through ordinary CPU loads and stores to addresses decoded by the device's BAR; on PCIe stores become posted Memory Writes and loads become non-posted Memory Reads.
PCIe interrupt mechanism in which the device signals an interrupt by a Memory Write of a per-vector data value to a per-vector address from its MSI-X table.
Specification (2.2 in the 2026 set) for out-of-band management of NVMe devices over MCTP on SMBus/I2C or PCIe VDMs, and in-band tunnelling through the admin queue.
Specification (1.4 in the 2026 set) for booting from NVMe, in particular NVMe over Fabrics, including the NBFT hand-off table.
I/O command set (1.5 in the 2026 set) in which a namespace is divided into zones written sequentially; adds Zone Append and Zone Management commands.
I/O command set (1.4 in the 2026 set) whose namespaces store values addressed by keys rather than LBAs.
I/O command set (1.3 in the 2026 set) defining compute namespaces and commands to load and execute programs on data in subsystem local memory.
The host-side PCIe component that connects the CPU and memory to the PCIe hierarchy, turning CPU MMIO accesses into requests and device DMA requests into memory accesses.
The Linux block layer framework that maps per-CPU software queues to hardware queue contexts; the NVMe driver maps each hardware context to an NVMe I/O queue pair.
PCIe capability and mechanism for logging and signalling correctable and uncorrectable errors.
NVMe mechanism (shared by all I/O command sets) by which hosts register with and acquire a namespace to coordinate access to a shared namespace across hosts; tied to the Host Identifier.
